Weekly Report
1. Norton indicated their willingness to accelerate their delivery schedule on delivering blades
with thicknesses ranging from 0.015 mil to 0.030 ml. Norton also agreed to formulate our
compositions, if needed.
Ni3 Al
2. We received NiA13 from Oak Ridge National Lab. for evaluation as a possible heater
material. A small piece was given to Willie for obtaining heaters by EDM technique. I
suggested cutting of the material using a Mo wire as opposed to a brass wire since Mo wire has a
high strength and can cut faster without much damage to the material. Another small piece of
the material will be sent Stony Brook for depositing Zirconia and NiAl. We will also be
sending a small piece to Alabama for laser cutting of serpentine blades.
3. Temperature measurement data obtained on integral heaters with and without the cartridges is
being analyzed.
4. Several heaters coated with nickel aluminide were pulsed during the last couple of weeks.
Heaters coated with 1 mil and 1.5 mil were pulsed at different energies to attain a maximum
temperature of 600C, 820℃, 10501150 C, and 1250C. Blades coated with 1 mil thick coating
survived 10,000 pulses at all the above temperatures except at 1150 ℃ and 1250C. In the case
of a blade heated to 1150℃, the blade survived for only 24 pulses, and a hot spot was noticed
after the third pulse. The blade broke into two pieces after the 24th pulse. The temperature at
the hot spot was more than 1250C. In the case of a blade heated to 1250℃, the blade twisted
and broke into two pieces after few pulses. Another blade was heated to 1250 C in a steady state
mode, and the blade exhibited creep behavoir in a minute, and showed intense hot spot for
several minutes before it broke into pieces within eight minutes. All these blades will be
examined using several techniques.
Heaters coated with 1.5 mil coating also showed roughly the same features as the 1.0 mil blade.
A 1 mil blade coated and heat treated in argon has shown no signs of failure even after 6000
pulses.
